$comment: THE ONE REGISTRY for the proposal system lab's knobs (the X-Bionic rework, 2026-10-10). Read by /test/proposal-system (TS import through lib/proposal-system/variants.ts) and by scripts/capture-proposal-system.mjs (readFileSync). TYPE IDS ARE LETTERS ONLY. THE FIRST VALUE OF EVERY KNOB IS PRODUCTION: PA is every knob at its first value and the control, byte-identical to /arcs/x-bionic/proposal; every other direction is one argument against it; PZ is ADR-155's whole answer at once. Since the merge with the X-Bionic branch (2026-10-10) the first values name the owner's picks there (the band, the case card, the layer opened, his three lines alone) and the second values are ADR-155's directions. When the owner picks, the winning values land on the production record and the losing branches are deleted with their guards (ADR-070 U35).

order.label: Order
order.note: current = the page as shipped. narrative = the owner's order of 10 October: about, the vision, the approach, where it plugs in, Loop, two brands, X-Bionic.

interstitial.label: Part opener
interstitial.note: callout = the owner's three lines, each alone on a screen (ADR-153 U4). quote = ADR-155's chapter band: the part ruler over the same line, numbered one to three.

jobHead.label: Job head
jobHead.note: band = ADR-153 U4's low gold band: the title and its mono line on the left, the job's one workstream on the right. mark = that one lit discipline first, the title one size down, the client, where it ran and the date as one mono line under it.

return.label: Loop's return
return.note: case = ADR-153 U5's case card: the record in the jobs' own housing, a lane per role. ledger = the same four rows as returns in the job's vocabulary: a value, a line, a tally.

approach.label: The approach
approach.note: handoff = ADR-153's three plates and two time bars. stack = one mono rail over the layer stack: the team on the organisation's slab, the layer appearing with its courses, Claude's runs along its edge. sheet, pinned and states = the owner's eight-step outline drawn as one run (ArcConfigRun): the vision's own layer with its four workstream tiles, creative production's tile opened onto its jobs, ads design worked through from its three inputs to the finished ad, the adopted run checked at every step, the skill and the evals written between the runs, and the automated run asking once. sheet reads it whole; pinned lights its six parts on a runway; states puts the handoff's rail over it, one state per pass.

upstream.label: Longer tasks
upstream.note: off = the approach beat carries the claim alone. horizon = a second beat on the owned horizon: the team's day upstream, the agent's run reaching up three times. lines = the owner's two lines (outline steps 7 and 8): a tool you operate, checked at every step, over an agent with the context and the evals, which runs much longer before it asks; the head carries the move upstream.

engine.label: The engine
engine.note: layer = ADR-153 U6, the layer opened: the gold slab the team writes, a lane per skill, X-Bionic's Claude Enterprise under it. pinned = ADR-154 U4's exploded stack on a runway, its slabs and callouts lighting one after another; the face is dropped, because a face and a pin never share a section.

directions.name: House
directions.question: the page as it ships, with the owner's picks of 10 October: does it already read as one argument?

directions.name: Narrative
directions.question: in the owner's order, with the vision first and the layer placed after the approach, does the page read top to bottom?
directions.shape: the reordered sections, every beat as shipped

directions.name: Chapter
directions.question: does a part open better under a numbered ruler than on its line alone?
directions.shape: three chapter bands, the same three lines under the part ruler

directions.name: Mark
directions.question: with one lit discipline and the proof cards' gold band, do the jobs read as the Loop cards' kin?
directions.shape: four jobs on the mark head

directions.name: Ledger
directions.question: do Loop's returns and the jobs' returns read as one language?

directions.name: Stack
directions.question: does the layer being written, drawn once, say that adoption and automation are one motion?
directions.shape: the approach on the stack figure

directions.name: Horizon
directions.question: does the longer-horizon claim need its own beat, or does the stack's run carry it?
directions.shape: the stack, then the owned horizon

directions.name: Pinned
directions.question: read in nine lit steps on a pinned runway, does the stack say more than the layer opened?
directions.shape: the engine as the exploded stack, pinned

directions.name: Run
directions.question: the owner's eight steps drawn as one run, read whole: does the configuration read in one look, from his layer to the finished ad?
directions.shape: the configuration as one sheet, then the two lines

directions.name: Run pinned
directions.question: the same run lit part by part on a pinned runway: does reading it in six steps tell the story better than the sheet?
directions.shape: the configuration on a runway, then the two lines

directions.name: Run states
directions.question: the same run under the handoff's rail, one state per pass: does clicking adoption, encoding, automation build it better than scrolling?
directions.shape: the configuration in three states, then the two lines

directions.name: The brief
directions.question: ADR-155's whole answer at once: one narrative, chapter bands, marked jobs, one return language, the stack, the pinned engine.
directions.shape: every knob at its second value, the horizon off

wave.note: 1470x830 is the owner's MacBook Air, the binding cell (ADR-153); 1440x790 the smaller Air; 1920x1200 where the 880px fill cap engages. Every beat is one screen by content bottom.
